cards.text: The LORD speaks to Ezekiel, His prophet, and calls him son of man. God has been picturing Samaria and Jerusalem as two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah (Ezekiel 23:4). Now He asks Ezekiel if he will pass judgment against them.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to declare to Oholah and Oholibah their abominations.

cards.text: So God lays out the charges, and friend, this is one of those moments I keep my mustache real still. First up, they have committed adultery.

cards.question: God says the two sisters committed adultery with their ___.
What did the sisters do with the children they bore to God?

cards.text: And God isn't done. He says they did this to Him too: on that very same day, they profaned His Sabbaths.

cards.question: On the very day the sisters slaughtered their children for their idols, they stayed far away from God's house.

cards.text: They went right into His sanctuary to profane it, inside His house. Then God speaks right to the sisters: they sent messengers for men who came from far away.

cards.question: When the men from far away arrive, how do the sisters greet them?

cards.text: Then the sisters sit on a couch of luxury, with a table spread out in front of it. And what's sitting on that table is NOT theirs to set out.

cards.question: What's the problem with what the sisters set on their luxury table?

answers.text: It's God's own incense and oil
It's food meant for the poor
It's a gift from their enemies

cards.text: A carefree crowd fills the place, and drunkards from the desert and men from the rabble put bracelets on their wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads. Friend, when THAT'S the guest list, I'm hiding the cookie boxes and turning off the porch light.

cards.question: God speaks of one of the sisters as "her who had grown old in adulteries." What does that phrase tell you about her?

answers.text: She's been unfaithful a long time
She's too old to be judged now

cards.text: Then God says of her, "Now let them use her as a prostitute, for that is all she is!" That one lands heavy, friend, so I'm taking my chef's hat off for a minute.
And the men sleep with Oholah and Oholibah as with a prostitute. But hold on, friend, because the scene turns, and righteous men step in to sentence them.

cards.question: Why do the righteous men sentence Oholah and Oholibah?

answers.text: They are adulteresses with blood on their hands
They broke their treaty with the Egyptians
They refused to pay tribute to Assyria

cards.text: Then the Lord GOD speaks, and friend, this is where I set the dough down: bring a mob against the sisters and hand them over to terror and plunder. The mob will stone them, cut them down with swords and kill their sons and daughters.

cards.question: Along with everything else, the mob will ___ the sisters' houses.
God says this judgment will put an end to indecency in the land and warn all the women not to imitate the sisters' behavior.
God's last word: the sisters will bear the consequences of their sins of idolatry. Then what will they know?

answers.text: That He is the Lord GOD

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "her who had grown old in adulteries.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the unseen wording of verse 37. Card 3 says only that the sisters committed adultery, so the earlier cards give no basis for reasoning out "idols" rather than "servants" or "rivals." This is a wording guess rather than a meaning-based blank.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
